senses.gloss: m., קֵהָה, קֵי׳ f. (preced.; cmp. כֵּהֶה) dull, faint;

(of cutting tools) blunt; (of teeth) blunt and loose.—Pl. קֵהִים, קֵהִין, קֵי׳; קֵהוֹת, קֵי׳. Midr. Sam. ch. XVI as with the grape vine כל מי … שיניו ק׳ וכ׳ he that eats of its unripe fruit, will have his teeth set on edge, so it is with Israel &c.; Lev. R. s. 36 (corr. version after Midr. Sam.).

units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 8:1:5">Y. Yoma VIII, 44ᵈ</cite> <he>בבא מן … ק׳ עליו</he> in the case of one that had come from a journey, and his feet were benumbed; Y. Ber. II, 5ᵇ bot.; a. e.

<cite ref="Taanit 7b:14">Taan. 7ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Ecclesiastes 10:10">Koh. X, 10</cite>) <he>אם ראית רקיע שק׳ כברזל וכ׳</he> when thou seest the sky as tough as iron not sending down dew or rain; Yalk. Koh. 979 <he>אם … דור שהשמים קהין וכ׳</he> when thou seest a generation over which the heavens are as tough &c.

Ab. IV, 20 ענבים קהות hard (unripe) grapes, opp. בשולות.—Trnsf. (of intellectual subjects) tough, difficult, unsolvable. Yalk. l. c. אם … שתלמודו ק׳ עליו כברזל when thou seest a student to whom his lesson is as tough as iron (Taan. 8ᵃ שלמודו קשה; Ms. M. כהה).

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 33:1">Pesik. R. s. 33</cite> <he>והמעשה שהיה ק׳ וכ׳</he> and when a case was too difficult for me to decide, I asked &c.; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 917:3">Yalk. Job 917</cite>.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:11:2">Cant. R. to IV, 11</cite>; a. e.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 4:6:8">Y. Shebi. IV, end, 35ᶜ</cite> <he>שכן דרך הק׳ אוכלות אותו</he> for craving women are in the habit of eating it (the unripe grape).
